REFERRED TO RACING, GAMING AND WAGERING
AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO RACING, GAMING AND WAGERING

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the racing, pari-mutuel wagering and breeding law and the workers' compensation law, in relation to the New York Jockey Injury Compensation Fund, Inc.
items.lawCode: Amd §221, RWB L; amd §§2, 11, 14-a, 18-a & 50, Work Comp L
items.lawSection: Racing, Pari-Mutuel Wagering and Breeding Law
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5541

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the racing, pari-mutuel wagering and breeding law and
the workers' compensation law, in relation to the New York Jockey Injury
Compensation Fund, Inc.

PURPOSE:

This bill would grant The New York Jockey Injury Compensation Fund, Inc.
the authority to limit the mandate to secure workers' compensation
insurance coverage to jockeys and apprentice jockeys.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Sections 1-2: Amend subdivisions 6 and 7 of section 221 of the Racing,
Pari-mutuel Wagering and Breeding Law to provide the New York Jockey
Injury Compensation Fund, Inc. the authority to limit the mandate to
secure workers' compensation insurance coverage only for jockeys and
apprentice jockeys.

Sections 3-9: Amend various sections of the Workers' Compensation Law to
provide that in the event the New York Jockey Injury Compensation Fund,
Inc. decided not to include exercise persons, they would be covered by
the workers' compensation policy maintained by the owner and/or trainer
who employs them.

Section 10: Effective date.

EXISTING LAW:

At present, The New York Jockey Injury Compensation Fund, Inc. is
required to secure workers' compensation insurance coverage for jockeys,
apprentice jockeys, and exercise persons, all licensed by the New York
State Gaming Commission (formerly the New York State Racing and Wagering
Board).

JUSTIFICATION:

In July 1990, the Legislature created The New York Jockey Injury Compen-
sation Fund, Inc. to provide workers' compensation insurance for jock-
eys, apprentice jockeys and exercise persons, all licensed by the New
York State Gaming Commission (formerly the New York State Racing and
Wagering Board) in an efficient manner at low cost. This legislation
grants The New York Jockey Injury Compensation Fund, Inc.  the authority
to limit the mandate to secure workers' compensation insurance coverage
only for jockeys and apprentice jockeys. This legislation will reduce
the cost of workers' compensation insurance premiums to The New York
Jockey Injury Compensation Fund, Inc.  Licensed exercise riders would be
covered by the workers' compensation policy maintained by the owner
and/or trainer who employs them. This is how such individuals were

covered before The New York Jockey Injury Compensation Fund, Inc. was
established. Since 2007, the statutory maximum indemnity payment has
doubled and the cost to The New York Jockey Injury Compensation Fund,
Inc. of obtaining workers' compensation insurance has more than tripled.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the State.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5541B

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the racing, pari-mutuel wagering and breeding law and
the workers' compensation law, in relation to the New York Jockey
Injury Compensation Fund, Inc.

 PURPOSE :

This bill would grant The New York Jockey Injury Compensation Fund,
Inc. the authority to self insure with the approval of the Gaming
Commission and to expand the workers they cover to included licensed
employees of licensed trainers.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Sections 1-2: Amend subdivisions 6 and 7 of section 221 of the Racing,
Pari-mutuel Wagering and Breeding Law to provide the New York Jockey
Injury Compensation Fund, Inc. the authority to, upon approval of the
Gaming Commission, to elect to self insure its workers' compensation
obligations.  Additionally these sections allow the New York Jockey
Injury Compensation Fund, Inc. the authority to, upon approval of the
Gaming Commission, expand their coverage to include licensed employees
of licensed trainers.

Sections 3-11: Amend various sections of the Workers' Compensation Law
to reflect the New York Jockey Injury Compensation Fund, Inc.'s
authority to expand their coverage to include licensed employees of
licensed trainers.

Section 12: Effective date.

 EXISTING LAW :

At present, The New York Jockey Injury Compensation Fund, Inc. is
required to secure workers' compensation insurance coverage for
jockeys, apprentice jockeys, and exercise persons, all licensed by the
New York State Gaming Commission (formerly the New York State Racing
and Wagering Board).

 JUSTIFICATION :

In July 1990, the Legislature created The New York Jockey Injury
Compensation Fund, Inc. to provide workers' compensation insurance for
jockeys, apprentice jockeys and exercise persons, all licensed by the
New York State Gaming Commission in an efficient manner at low cost.
This legislation grants the fund the authority, upon approval from the
Gaming Commission, to expand their ability to secure workers'
compensation insurance coverage to include licensed employees of
licensed trainers. Since 2007, due to significant statutory increases
in indemnity payments, the cost to fund of obtaining workers'
compensation insurance has almost quadrupled. This bill will grant the
fund the option to elect a form of self-insurance to meet its workers'
compensation insurance obligations if, in their opinion, self-insuring
would enable it to do so at a lower cost than procuring a policy in
the market.

Additionally, this bill would give the fund, upon the approval of the
Gaming Commission, the option to elect to expand the mandate to secure
workers' compensation insurance for licensed employees of licensed
trainers. At present, licensed employees of licensed trainers are
covered by the workers' compensation policy of their respective
trainers which results, for example, in an exercise rider and hot
walker who work together for the same trainer at the track being
covered by different workers' compensation policies. Therefore, the
ability to expand the scope of the fund to secure workers'
compensation insurance coverage for licensed employees of licensed
trainers could make coverage more efficient. Potentially expanding the
number of individuals covered by the fund should also improve their
bargaining power when seeking a policy in the commercial market.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to the State.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
